text:
asha: Heads-up — KiteWave (AE POC) wants to bring a customer-finetuned model called `wavecore-13b-ft` for a 4-week POC. They need private deploy (VPC), customer-managed KMS, and 50 rps peak with 100ms tail-latency SLO for short convo flows. Asking: catalog fit, variant recommendations, any infra/security blockers?

leo: quick q — what format are they providing the model in? HF `gguf`/PyTorch/ONNX? Also any custom tokenizer/BPE?

asha: They pushed a tar with `model.gguf`, `tokenizer.json`, and a small adapter checkpoint. Tokenizer is custom BPE (not standard llama). They said they'd prefer deterministic outputs (no sampling) and need an embeddings endpoint too.

priya: Thanks. Two immediate things: 1) custom tokenizer requires our tokenization compatibility check before catalog onboarding. 2) For embeddings + gen we should consider two routes: a smaller embed-only variant and the 13B for generation. Pricing note: if we run full 13B on Dedicated gpus at that throughput expect committed capacity. I'll draft a ballpark.

leo: From runtime perspective, custom tokenizer means we need to validate: token ids, special tokens, pad/eos handling. If tokenizer maps differ we can create a token-mapping shim but it adds latency. Also `gguf` is supported — good. For deterministic responses set `temperature=0` and disable top_p sampling. That’s fine.

 tom: Infra note: 50 rps at ~100ms TTF is aggressive for 13B on single-GPU unless we do aggressive batching and KV cache. Options: 1) Dedicated pool with model pinned and batching tuned; 2) Hybrid route: host embeddings on a smaller model (7B) and gen on 13B with autoscaling bursts. Also need to confirm memory footprint (fp16 vs 8-bit). If they accept 8-bit quant we can reduce GPU memory ~40% and cheaper hosts.

deploy-bot: [catalog-scan] initial artifact scan complete — tokenizer.json present, relative vocab size 48k, unknown special token markers: [<|pad|> missing]. Suggest token-check. Model file `model.gguf` appears loadable.

priya: Security & compliance: they attached a vendor security questionnaire and SOC2 cert in the email. @tom can you confirm the KMS policy needs? For Private deploy we'll require a Key ARN with cross-account policy for our deployer role OR customer-managed agent.

 tom: Correct — for Private we need a KMS key policy that allows Redwood deploy role Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey. If they want HSM, escalate to security. Also we need network egress rules for pullers.

asha: Customer also asked about model fallbacks if GPU capacity saturates. Can we offer an automatic fallback to a quantized 7B variant?

leo: Yes — we can build a fallback policy: route to `wavecore-7b-compact` with lower-cost latency SLO. Need to verify dev-provided 7B variant or we produce a distilled variant. Fallback will change output distribution — call that out in SOW.

priya: I'll note in the POC SOW: (a) Tokenizer validation + small shim if needed, (b) Dedicated capacity recommendation for stable latency, (c) fallback to 7B variant with explicit QA of regressions, (d) security questionnaire review and KMS policy.

asha: Example minimal deploy config I suggested to them:```
model: wavecore-13b-ft
format: gguf
precision: int8
deploy_mode: dedicated
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 6
batching: { max_tokens: 2048, dynamic_window_ms: 5 }
kms_key_arn: <customer-key-arn>
```

leo: That looks good. For the tokenizer check we can run this quick script (run locally):```bash
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json'); print(t.encode('hello world').ids)"
```

deploy-bot: [ticket] Created: #SW-4521 "KiteWave POC — tokenizer + catalog onboarding" assigned to priya, leo, tom. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/SW-4521

asha: Perfect — next steps: Priya to own security triage + SOW draft, Leo to run tokenizer compatibility and small regression eval, Tom to confirm infra sizing and KMS policy. I'll loop in the customer with the proposed plan. :+1:

priya: On it. Will upload security notes and SOW draft by EOD tomorrow.

leo: Will run tokenizer checks now and post quick mismatch report.

tom: I'll return sizing numbers and a rough pricing delta (8-bit vs fp16) within 24h.

asha: Thanks team — ping me in thread for any blocker. :eyes:
